title: Touring with Louis Jordan: Apollo, Savoy, Detroit and the Moe Gale offer
summary: After ten weeks in Chicago they tour with Louis Jordan and play the Apollo, Detroit and Cincinnati, but decline Moe Gale's one-sided contract.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, Murray, yeah. We had him. On trombone --
Of course, running. I was just come down from Great Lakes.

You come down from Great Lakes. We had a good-sounding band, because we played there, we played in Chicago ten weeks. And then we were offered a tour with Louis Jordan. The tour took us into New York to play Apollo Polly Theater. And from Apollo Polly Theater into Washington, D.C.
Around the Horn. (Unintelligible) [Theater]-ed. Around the Horn, Howard, see.
(Unintelligible) And then we left there and we played -- we left Louis -- oh, that was the time we played Chicago. Were you with the band when we played Chicago, Charles?
I was still in the Navy.
You were in the Navy when we played --

That's right. Because we were booked in Chicago at the Savoy Ballroom. And -- because Stuff Smith was playing in Chicago and he came out to -- and Jonah Joe Jones. Jonah Joe Jones was playing with Stuff Smith at the time, and they came out to hear the band, see. And we played at the Savoy
Ballroom to a nice crowd, to a real nice crowd. It wasn't no knockdown, dragout crowd, but a real good crowd. // (End of Tape #9.)

We left there and went to Cincinnati, Ohio. No, we left there and went to Detroit, and played a theater there with Louis Jordan. We met Louis Jordan there, and we followed Lena Horne. And we played the theater in Detroit. Then we left Detroit, and came on down to Cincinnati, where we played the Jabberwocks. Our band had always been quite popular around Cincinnati. We played the Delta's Jabberwocks there. And they had a packed house, at Tapp Auditorium. And then we brought the band on back to St. Louis. That's all the booking we had.

In the meantime, while out in New York, they wanted to sign us up. Moe Gale and Mr. Buchanan, (Unintelligible) who was running the Savoy Ballroom for the Mogail people, wanted to sign us up. But like I told you, in the contract everything's in their favor. And nothing in our favor. So we decided to come on back to St. Louis. And in the meantime, we had I think a three weeks booking at the Club Plantation, shortly before it closed. And before that, we went into the Tunetown Ballroom. We had a week's booking in the Tunetown Ballroom. And that kept us pretty busy, the rest of that summer.
